title: Default seccomp profile: socket deny rules for AF_VSOCK & NETLINK_AUDIT can be bypassed by setting high bits in the argument
body:
The AF_VSOCK deny rule added in #575 "to prevent container escapes via VM sockets" can be bypassed. Seccomp compares syscall arguments as 64-bit values, but the kernel's `socket(int domain, int type, int protocol)` drops the upper 32 bits. `socket(0x100000028, SOCK_STREAM, 0)` doesn't match `arg0==40`, so it falls through to the `arg0!=40` allow  rule. The kernel then truncates the family to 40 and opens a vsock socket.

The same applies to the older socket rule for NETLINK_AUDIT (applies without CAP_AUDIT_WRITE). 

Reproduced on x86_64 with podman v6.1.3 on Fedora 45 Beta:

```
sudo podman run --rm --cap-drop AUDIT_WRITE --security-opt label=disable docker.io/library/python:3 python3 -c 'import ctypes as  c;l=c.CDLL(None,use_errno=True);[print(hex(f),t,hex(p),l.syscall(41,c.c_ulong(f),t,c.c_ulong(p))) for f,t,p in((16,3,9),(16,3,0x100000009),(40,1,0),(0x100000028,1,0))]'
```

Output:
 
```
  0x10 3 0x9 -1
  0x10 3 0x100000009 3
  0x28 1 0x0 -1
  0x100000028 1 0x0 4
```

`label=disable` is to show seccomp's behaviour. With SELinux enabled, the vsock call returned EACCES, which comes from the LSM and not from seccomp. So on SELinux hosts the LSM is what blocks it. On hosts without a confining LSM, the seccomp rule is the only protection and it doesn't work.
